correctness.rationale: Exact monomial Gram matrix splits by degree modulo m, giving positive Schur pivots h_j. The stable Riccati root H(x) has a directly verified first correction E_m(x)=2m|a|²lambda²x³/Delta(x)². Uniform diagonal lower bounds and |a|<1/2 provide a strict Lipschitz contraction, so an O(\(n^{-2}\)) local residual remains O(\(n^{-2}\)) at j=n. The proof covers every fixed m, complex a and lambda>0; 120 exact Gram checks and 12 asymptotic tests supplement, but do not replace, this proof.

value.rationale: The \(n^{-2}\) critical balanced Sobolev scaling is a published natural boundary. The explicit universal leading norm cannot distinguish different single-harmonic positive densities indexed by m, but the newly obtained first correction detects m exactly linearly and is strictly positive. This provides a principled finite-degree benchmark for strong asymptotics across an entire motivated family, not an arbitrary slice or computation.
